You are going to turn a recipe into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Weekday Lentil Soup and Salad for Four for 4 people
Resource limits: one cook, two burners, one toaster oven, one stick blender.
Everything must be finished by 12:30.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Weekday Lentil Soup and Salad for Four

Lunch at half past twelve. One cook, two burners, one toaster oven, one stick blender. Nothing here is fussy; the only real constraint is that the cook can stand in one place at a time, so the salad and the bread wait until the soup is quietly simmering.

Soup
Dice an onion, a carrot and two sticks of celery; 8 minutes. Sweat them in oil with a bay leaf for 10 minutes. Stir in the rinsed lentils, a spoonful of tomato paste and a litre of stock; 3 minutes. Simmer until the lentils are soft, 25 to 40 minutes. Blitz a third of the pot with the stick blender and stir it back in; 4 minutes. Season it, then keep it at a bare simmer until you sit down.

Salad
Start the salad once the soup is simmering. Wash and spin the leaves; 5 minutes. Shave the fennel and the radishes thin; 7 minutes. Whisk the lemon, oil and mustard in the bottom of the bowl; 3 minutes. Five minutes after the soup goes back on the heat, dress and toss the salad; 2 minutes. Dressed any earlier and the leaves collapse.

Bread
Cut the loaf into thick slices once the soup is simmering; 3 minutes. Warm them in the toaster oven for 8 minutes. Wrap the warm bread in a cloth and leave it on the table.

Table
Lay four places once the bread is wrapped; 5 minutes. When the soup, the salad and the bread are all ready, carry the pot and the bowl through together; 3 minutes.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

This plan is for a weekday lunch serving four people: a lentil soup, a green salad, and warm thick-cut bread, with everything ready to sit down by 12:30. The setup has only one cook, two burners, one toaster oven, and one stick blender, so the work must be staged around the cook’s single location; the salad and bread are deliberately started after the soup is quietly simmering. The soup requires a variable simmer until the lentils are soft, then a brief blended portion returned to the pot and held at a bare simmer. The salad ingredients may be prepared early, but the leaves must not be dressed until five minutes after the soup goes back on the heat, because dressing earlier makes them collapse. The bread is sliced during the soup simmer, toasted, wrapped, and left on the table; the table is laid only after the bread is wrapped, and the final serving steps happen only when the soup, salad, and bread are all ready.

A track is one sequential line of work, so steps in the same track are chained and never overlap; if two things must happen at the same time, they belong in different tracks. A step has exactly one duration kind: fixed with `seconds`, variable with `minSeconds`, `maxSeconds`, and `defaultSeconds`, or indefinite until the person ends it. A `startTrigger` places a step against the clock or against another step, using `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`, or `compound`. Step IDs are unique across the whole program, not just within a track. Every `task` referenced by a step needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry’s `maxConcurrent` is what stops two steps from sharing one burner, one toaster oven, or one stick blender. Work repeated `n` times belongs on one step using `replicates`, with `instances: "each"` for per-repetition follow-ups, `instances: "all"` for the barrier, and `maxInFlight` when a holding area only fits some repetitions at once.

For this recipe, I expect to declare these resource constraints, with one person working overall:

- `prep`: `maxConcurrent: 1` — the single cook’s hands-on station; one person is working.
- `burner`: `maxConcurrent: 2` — two stovetop burners are available; one person is working.
- `toaster-oven`: `maxConcurrent: 1` — one toaster oven for the bread; one person is working.
- `stick-blender`: `maxConcurrent: 1` — one stick blender for the soup; one person is working.

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
